constitutional_basis: Article XXVI (ACTUAL external solver, not reimplementation)

svMultiPhysics_execution.binary: svmultiphysics (242MB ELF, extracted from Docker simvascular/solver:latest layer 14)
svMultiPhysics_execution.mpi: OpenMPI 5.0.10 (installed via micromamba, user-level, no root)
svMultiPhysics_execution.test_case: pipe_RCR_3d (official svFSI-Tests case: 3D pipe with RCR boundary conditions)
svMultiPhysics_execution.convergence: 5 iterations per time step, converged at every step

svMultiPhysics_results.interpretation: Physically realistic cardiovascular pressure response to pulsatile inlet flow. The RCR boundary condition creates the expected windkessel behavior.

P-01_cross_check.comparison: NOT directly comparable — our 1D model assumed steady-state, svMultiPhysics used pulsatile inlet flow. The 3D solver shows the pressure drop oscillates with the flow waveform, which the 1D model cannot capture.
P-01_cross_check.what_this_validates: The svMultiPhysics solver WORKS in this environment. It produces physically realistic 3D Navier-Stokes solutions with RCR boundary conditions. The solver can now be used for P-01's actual multi-segment shunt geometry.
P-01_cross_check.what_remains: Build P-01 multi-segment shunt 3D mesh. Run svMultiPhysics on it. Compare to 1D model at matched conditions (steady-state or matched pulsatile).
